Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · School & learning

article noun

in a newspaper or magazine

also articles, newspaper article, magazine article

classical

Traupman 273, 351
M-O s.v. genre: article
Plin. NH 8.44 (Lewis & Short)

commentātiō, commentātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an article, a short written study

Classically a careful study, and from the elder Pliny on a written treatise (Lewis & Short); Gellius calls the chapters of his Noctēs Atticae commentātiōnēs (praef. 4). Traupman gives it for a newspaper article (p. 351).

Other words

  • 1commentāriolum: neuter (Traupman 273 commentāriolus m., which Lewis & Short finds only in Jerome). Q. Cic. Pet. 58: volō enim hoc commentāriolum petītiōnis habērī omnī ratiōne perfectum. Lewis & Short s.v. commentāriolum: masculine only in Hier. Ep. 149.1.

    commentāriolum1, commentāriolī n. — a short piece of writing, a sketch

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Q. Cic. Pet. 58; Traupman 273

  • opusculum, opusculī n. — a little work

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Parad. prooem. 5 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. genre: article

  • articulus, articulī m. — a joint; a member of a sentence; the grammatical article

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Levi–Bini p. 7; Traupman 273 (the grammatical article)

    A false friend, though Levi–Bini gives it beside caput for the article of a newspaper: classically a joint or a knuckle, a member of a sentence, and in the jurists a short clause (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quoniam longinquīs per hiemem noctibus in agrō … terrae Atticae commentātiōnēs hāsce lūdere ac facere exōrsī sumus, idcircō eās īnscrīpsimus Noctium esse Atticārum

    since I began to write these pieces for my own amusement in the long winter nights in the country in Attica, I have called them Attic NightsGell. praef. 4
